newsitem.title: USA: Schwab to offer private money managers - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Schwab to offer private money managers - WSJ.

text.p: Discount brokerage services company Charles Schwab Corp is starting a program to offer investors a way to hire private money managers, the Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday.

The company's customers will have access to private institutional money managers, including Dreman Value Advisors, Lazard Freres Asset Management, Navellier & Associates, Nicholas Applegate Capital Management, Van Kampen American Capital, Weiss, Peck & Greer, Delaware Capital Management and Boston Co, the paper said.
The private money managers will put an investor's into a separate account and use it to buy and sell individual securities, the report said.
Mutual funds pool an investor's money with that of other investors.
The paper said the company is expected to announce the program today.
